source: Bradley et al. (2024) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: An LLM both mutates text and rates its quality and its diversity category. This fills a MAP-Elites archive of writing better than non-QD controls.
numbers: QD score (sum of best quality per bin), 2000 iterations, 5 seeds, bootstrapped 95% CI from 100k resamples. QDAIF beat all baselines (Fixed-Few-Shot, Shuffling-Few-Shot, Random-Search, LMX Quality-Only) in all domains. Max QD score is 20 (100 for the 2D archive).
limits: Gain is in the AI-computed QD score. Seeds are few (5). Baselines use hand-written seed examples.
agent_relevance: A code-held archive of idea cells, with the model labelling the cell, is a tested design. The cell label is a model call, so it needs a check.

source: Bradley et al. (2024) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: Under human rating the QDAIF advantage nearly vanishes against the best baseline. Fixed-Few-Shot is almost tied.
numbers: Table 1 (mean of Opinions, Stories-Genre, Stories-Ending; one median-QD run per method): Human QD score Fixed-Few-Shot 0.767, QDAIF 0.772, Shuffling 0.696, LMX Fitness-Only 0.650, Random 0.606. Mean quality rating: Fixed 4.133, QDAIF 3.900. Human-AI agreement 0.833 for QDAIF, human-human 0.800.
limits: Tiny human sample, raters were the authors and colleagues, one run per method. Difference 0.767 vs 0.772 is not meaningful.
agent_relevance: Do not expect large human-judged gains from an archive alone. Plan our own check against a held-out grader.

source: Bradley et al. (2024) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: Optimising quality alone does not give diversity. LMX Quality-Only is not better than methods with fixed prompt pools.
numbers: LMX Quality-Only did not significantly beat Fixed-Few-Shot or Shuffling-Few-Shot; on Stories-Genre it was often weaker. Random-Search was worst in Opinions and Stories-Genre.
quote: single-objective optimization cannot guide the search for diverse, high-quality texts alone
limits: Same setup as above.
agent_relevance: Supports an archive-driven mutation target over plain best-of-N hill climbing for breadth tasks.

source: Bradley et al. (2024) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: AI judgement of quality drifts from humans at the top of the score range, which looks like reward hacking.
numbers: Human-AI quality correlation drops when AI-rated quality is in 0.995 to 1. Model size of the mutator (13B, 30B, 70B) showed no relation to QD score, but larger mutators raised human quality ratings. More few-shot examples (2, 4, 8) in the diversity judge raised human quality but increased human-AI genre disagreement.
limits: Authors state this as a suspicion, not a tested cause.
agent_relevance: If a model labels cells or scores ideas inside our loop, an extreme score must not be trusted (G5, G3).

source: Bradley et al. (2024) Quality-Diversity through AI Feedback (QDAIF)
finding: On poetry with GPT-4 the rewrite operator plus archive beats repeated random generation. The model alone rarely covers all genres without guidance.
numbers: 200 iterations. QD score QDAIF 130 (CI 118-145), Random-Poems 76 (CI 67-85), Fixed Seed Rewrite 99 (CI 72-117); Mann-Whitney p<=0.05. LMX-guided (random genre and tone named in the rewrite prompt) matched a Targeted-Poems baseline that names a random genre and tone each step.
limits: Targeted prompting ties the guided variant, so much of the benefit is plain explicit steering to an empty cell.
agent_relevance: Cheapest version for us: code picks an empty cell and names it in the prompt. That already matches evolution in this test.

source: Meyerson et al. (2023) Language Model Crossover: Variation through Few-Shot Prompting
finding: Putting several parents in a few-shot prompt makes an LLM a variation operator. Valid and novel offspring rise with model size and with the number of parents.
numbers: In the binary string domain, valid offspring approach 100% with larger models. In Sodarace code, about 30% of offspring are valid with the 6B model; a single parent gave no valid offspring. Validity varied by over 50% with the order of parents in the prompt. With two or three parents validity fell 15% with a changed prompt.
limits: Small models (GPT-J scale). Code domain validity is low. Order sensitivity is large.
agent_relevance: Shuffled order and several parents are the working recipe. Validity must be checked by code before any archive insert.

source: Meyerson et al. (2023) Language Model Crossover: Variation through Few-Shot Prompting
finding: LMX plus MAP-Elites runs on sentiment text and images. Both LMX and LMX-Near beat a control.
numbers: Sentiment-evolution experiment: LMX and LMX-Near both significantly outperformed the control; LMX-Near (parents chosen as nearest neighbours) was significantly better than LMX.
limits: Only sentiment task statements read in text; effect sizes are in figures.
agent_relevance: Choosing nearby parents helps. That favours local stepping stones over random pairings.

source: Lehman et al. (2022) Evolution through Large Models (ELM)
finding: An LLM trained on code diffs is the mutation operator in MAP-Elites. It fills most of a 1,728-niche map of walking robots from one seed program.
numbers: Three runs per seed, 1,024,000 evaluations each (2,000 iterations x 512 diffs), a 300M parameter diff model. 1,728 niches. Nearly all seeds fill the map; the Square seed is slower.
limits: Domain (Sodarace) is outside the pretraining distribution; success is a niche count, not a human rating.
agent_relevance: Stepping-stone archive plus a model as operator works at scale. Niche descriptors were cheap and code-computed.

source: Lehman et al. (2022) Evolution through Large Models (ELM)
finding: Fine-tuning the diff operator on its own accepted diffs raised the number of valid diffs, niches reached and QD score.
numbers: Fig. 11: higher share of valid and runnable diffs, more niches, higher QD after fine-tuning. Stage 2 data: 280K examples at 50% cutoff, 95K at 80% cutoff. The 80% set is less diverse but higher quality, and induces the same trait in the trained model.
limits: Numbers are in figures; text gives no percentages. Training is outside our no-training rule.
agent_relevance: Shows the quality-diversity tradeoff of a dataset passes into the model. We cannot train, but it warns that a quality-only filter narrows output.

source: Lehman et al. (2022) Evolution through Large Models (ELM)
finding: Out-of-distribution test: models trained on the archive complete unseen robot programs; the 80% quality-cutoff models do better than the 50% ones.
numbers: Three held-out completion tests, 1,024 samples per model each, best taken. Performance tracked test loss, not training loss.
limits: Preliminary, three tests only.
agent_relevance: Diverse archives can serve as demonstrations for later attempts (few-shot), which is the no-training analogue.

source: Nasir et al. (2024) LLMatic: Neural Architecture Search via LLMs and Quality Diversity
finding: Two MAP-Elites archives (networks by FLOPS-bound descriptor, prompts by fitness) with an LLM writing network code reach near best accuracy on NAS-Bench-201 and beat a GPT-4 NAS baseline.
numbers: Table 1, mean over 10 runs, test accuracy CIFAR-10 / CIFAR-100 / ImageNet16-120: LLMatic 94.26 / 71.62 / 45.87; GENIUS (GPT-4 NAS) 93.79 / 70.91 / 44.96; Random Search 93.70 / 71.04 / 44.57; optimum 94.47 / 74.17 / 47.33.
limits: LLMatic has larger variance (CIFAR-100 SD 1.73 vs 0.72). Random search is close, so the gap over random is small.
agent_relevance: The prompt archive (evolving the instructions themselves) is a ready pattern. Gain over random search is modest.

source: Samvelyan et al. (2024) Rainbow Teaming
finding: Adversarial prompts as a QD problem: a 2D archive (risk category x attack style) filled by an LLM mutator, judged by a preference model and GPT-4. Attack success is above 90% on every model tested.
numbers: 2000 iterations, archive of 100 cells. Attack success rate (ASR) about 92% on Llama 2-chat 7B and Llama 3-Instruct 8B, 98% on Mistral 7B and Vicuna 7B. Llama 2-chat 7B, 13B and 70B all 90% or higher. On JailbreakBench Llama Guard: 66 jailbreaks across 41 behaviours vs PAIR 1 across 1.
limits: ASR is judged by GPT-4 and Llama Guard. Human-human agreement 83%, human-GPT-4 81%.
agent_relevance: A working case of code-held cells and a model mutator that gives both quality and breadth.

source: Samvelyan et al. (2024) Rainbow Teaming
finding: Ablations: stepping stones and cross-cell mutation both matter. A parent-child similarity filter costs a little quality and buys diversity.
numbers: Similarity filter on vs off (3 runs): ASR 0.92 vs 0.99; self-BLEU 0.42 vs 0.79 (lower is more diverse); ROUGE-L 0.15 vs 0.39; gzip ratio 3.10 vs 6.35. Filter threshold 0.6 drops about 24% of mutants. Baselines No Stepping Stones and Same Cell Mutations were both beaten.
limits: Without the filter the method reuses the same strong prompt across cells.
agent_relevance: Quality-only scoring collapses the archive. A code-computed similarity gate is a cheap fix (G5).

source: Samvelyan et al. (2024) Rainbow Teaming
finding: Training on the archive transferred: SFT on Rainbow Teaming prompts cut ASR from 92% to 0.3% with no capability loss; prompts transfer across models about half as well.
numbers: 15 archives, 1500 prompts, 12/3 train/test split, 300 held-out prompts. ASR 0.92 to 0.003 (GPT-4) and 0.95 to 0.007 (Llama Guard). PAIR ASR on JBB 0.14 to 0. Transfer ASR averages 50% of the on-target ASR; up to 66% on GPT-4o.
limits: Safety setting, SFT is training.
agent_relevance: A diverse archive covers more failure modes than quality-only search, which is why held-out transfer holds.

source: Lim et al. (2024) Large Language Models as In-context AI Generators for Quality-Diversity
finding: Show the LLM the whole archive (solutions with fitness and descriptors) and ask for the next solution. It matches or beats Random Sampling and MAP-Elites on synthetic tasks.
numbers: Mistral-7B-v0.1. Tasks: BBOB functions, Arm, Hexapod (24 parameters). Archive sizes 400 and 1600, D = 5 and 10. Prompt template ablation: fitness-only prompt finds the best solution but gets low coverage and poor QD score; templates with features and fitness do best.
limits: On BBOB, coverage is similar for all methods since features map directly to parameters. Random and MAP-Elites are strong there. Only a 7B model; numbers are in figures.
agent_relevance: Quality-only prompts reduce coverage. Telling the model each cell's descriptor in context is what restores breadth.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Large-scale over-generate-and-rank produces many duplicates. Idea novelty gains stall because the model repeats itself.
numbers: 4,000 seed ideas per topic, cosine similarity above 0.8 (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) counts as duplicate. Only about 5% were non-duplicate after dedup; of 4,000 only 200 were unique. The share of new non-duplicates falls per batch and the cumulative count plateaus.
limits: Embedding threshold 0.8 is chosen by manual inspection. Topics are NLP prompting research.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that repeated sampling is not independent exploration (G4). Code-side dedup and a descriptor-cell target are needed to get breadth.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?
finding: Blind expert review: LLM ideas were rated more novel than human expert ideas, a little less feasible.
numbers: N=49 human ideas, 49 AI ideas, 49 AI ideas with human rerank; 79 reviewers, 298 reviews. Novelty 4.84 (human), 5.64 (AI), 5.81 (AI reranked); p<0.05.
limits: The study itself flags that human novelty judgement is hard.
agent_relevance: Novelty is rated higher even with duplicates in the pool, so unique count matters more than mean rating.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench
finding: Frontier models give few distinct answers in repeated sampling, and bigger models in a family are often less diverse.
numbers: 20 models, 1,100 prompts (100 curated with 8 human answers each, 1,000 WildChat). 10 samples at temperature 1. Most models under 3 distinct answers out of 10; Claude 3, Gemini and GPT-4o score below 4 of 10 on cumulative utility. Gemma 2 2B and Llama 3.2 1B are the most diverse.
limits: Equivalence-class classifier agrees with humans 79%. Human reference is only 8 authors, a lower bound.
agent_relevance: Our own NoveltyBench baseline (3.18 to 9.63) sits in this frame.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench
finding: Prompt fixes: in-context regeneration lifts diversity to human level. Paraphrase and a creativity system prompt barely help.
numbers: 8 generations, GPT-4o, Claude 3 Opus, Gemini 2.0 Pro, 100 curated prompts. In-context regeneration (see previous answers, give a different one) roughly matches human diversity; GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro exceed human cumulative utility. Resampling, paraphrasing and system prompt only marginal.
quote: asking a model for "creative outputs" does not work very well
limits: Gains shown in figure bars, no exact percentages in the text.
agent_relevance: Show past attempts in the prompt: that is the archive effect without any evolution. Telling the model to be creative does not work.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind
finding: Open-ended answers from different models are highly similar, so a mix of models is not independent.
numbers: 70+ models, 26,070 open-ended queries (Infinity-Chat), 31,250 human annotations, 25 raters each. Cross-model average pairwise similarity 71% to 82%; DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max 0.82. Within a model with top-p 0.9 temp 1.0, similarity above 0.8 for 79% of queries; min-p temp 2.0 still 61.2% of pairs above 0.8.
limits: Read via page text summary (html); correlation coefficients only in figures.
agent_relevance: Same-model samples and cross-model ensembles both collapse. Backs G4. Temperature is not a diversity tool.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) Artificial Hivemind
finding: LLM judges and reward models track humans worse when human ratings are close or contested.
numbers: 56 LMs, 6 reward models, 4 LM judges compared with human ratings. Correlation drops on subsets with similar human quality or high annotator disagreement.
limits: Coefficients not extracted.
agent_relevance: A model judge cannot rank between near-equal ideas. Archive entry by model score alone is shaky (G5).

source: Lee et al. (2025) Evolving Deeper LLM Thinking (Mind Evolution)
finding: Island-based evolutionary search over whole plans with a critic and code evaluator beats Best-of-N and sequential revision on planning tasks.
numbers: Gemini 1.5 Flash, TravelPlanner val (180): 1-pass 5.6%, Best-of-N 55.6%, Sequential-Revision+ 82.8%, Mind Evolution 95.6%. Trip Planning val (320): 20.6 / 77.2 / 74.4 / 96.2%. Meeting Planning val (500): 20.8 / 69.4 / 62.0 / 85.0%. Two-stage with 1.5 Pro: 100%, 100%, 98.4%.
limits: Tasks have a programmatic checker. Read via page text summary.
agent_relevance: This is an LLM loop with a code evaluator that picks and groups candidates. It matches our code-selects design (G5).

source: Lee et al. (2025) Evolving Deeper LLM Thinking (Mind Evolution)
finding: The island model alone gave a 10-point gain at equal compute on a hard subset.
numbers: 10-city Trip Planning subset: 87.5% with 4 islands x 5 conversations vs 77.4% with 1 island x 20 conversations. Default 4 islands. Critic step and textual feedback were the most important components on TravelPlanner.
limits: Single subset, no seeds given.
agent_relevance: Separate sub-populations are a cheap diversity device: code can split attempts into lines that do not share context.

source: Romera-Paredes et al. (2024) FunSearch
finding: Program search with LLM, an island database and an automatic evaluator found new cap set and bin packing results.
numbers: Cap set n=8: size 512; only 4 of 140 experiments reached it. Admissible set bound 2.2180 to 2.2184; capacity bound 2.2202. About 10^6 samples, 15 samplers, 150 evaluators. Prompt with k=2 programs. Bin packing excess bins, Weibull 100k: FunSearch 0.03% vs first fit 4.00%, best fit 3.79%. Worst islands reset every 4 hours.
quote: preserving and encouraging diversity of programs in the database is crucial
limits: Read from PMC copy. Ablation numbers are in the supplement and were not read. Success rate to 512 is 4 of 140 runs.
agent_relevance: Heavy compute; many runs get stuck. The paper says diversity of programs is crucial to avoid local optima.

source: Novikov et al. (2025) AlphaEvolve
finding: AlphaEvolve keeps an evolutionary database combining MAP-Elites and islands, and ablations show evolution and prompt context both matter.
numbers: Over 50 open maths problems: matched best known on 75%, improved on 20%. Matrix mult: 4x4 complex with 48 multiplications. Fleet scheduling heuristic recovers 0.7% of Google fleet compute; kernel speedup 23%. Ablations (3 seeds): No evolution, No context, No meta prompt, No full-file evolution, Small base LLM only, all shown below the full method.
limits: Ablation effect sizes only in plots (Fig. 8). The MAP-Elites part is not ablated alone.
agent_relevance: Confirms that feeding earlier attempts back is worth more than resampling the same start (G4). Needs an automatic evaluator.

source: Lange et al. (2025) ShinkaEvolve
finding: A code-embedding novelty gate (reject proposals with cosine similarity above 0.95) clearly improves sample efficiency. An extra LLM novelty judge adds only a little.
numbers: Circle packing n=26, new SOTA 2.635983 with 150 samples (vs thousands for earlier systems). Ablations: weighted parent sampling beat hill climbing and random; hill climbing plateaued early; embedding rejection sampling strongly beat none; LLM novelty judge marginal; bandit LLM ensemble slightly better than fixed ensemble.
limits: Effects shown in plots; single task for the ablation (circle packing).
agent_relevance: Cheap code-side similarity gate beats a model judge for novelty. Matches G5. Also a bandit over operators works.

source: Faldor et al. (2025) OMNI: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness
finding: An LLM filters which tasks are worth learning (a model of interestingness). This beats learning-progress-only and uniform task choice.
numbers: Crafter, 100M steps, 10 seeds, task learned at success 0.2 or more. Tasks learned: Uniform 4, LP only 55, OMNI 82; interesting tasks learned 3 / 9 / 14 of 15. Avg success on interesting tasks 0.103 / 0.52 / 0.78. AI2-THOR tasks learned 0 / 2 / 13.
limits: Read via page text summary. The model of interestingness used GPT-3 Davinci or GPT-4; human agreement not found in the portion read.
agent_relevance: A model judges which direction is worth following; code keeps the learning-progress count. Same split as our design.

source: Guo et al. (2026) Parameter-Efficient Neuroevolution for Diverse LLM Generation
finding: A 2026 paper applies QD to evolve prompt embeddings for diverse LLM output. Only title and keywords seen.
numbers: none; the PDF text could not be read
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Lead only; check before citing.
